lines: scene_direction

Rain beads on the black gravel before Leto's Manor. The great door stands open, brass handles worn bright. Four cloaks glisten under it.

Chadwick, Leena, Vigil, and Sodacan Bob stop on the same stone step. Each feels the others, a thin pull behind the ribs, like a bell struck in another room.

Candles burn in the hall, tall and steady. A steward waits with a silver tray, his eyes moving from one to the other. He bows low.

"You are early. All four. Please."
character_reply

*draws his sword* 

This is the way. Sorensen Leto. Now.
character_reply
Where is Sorensen Leto? Speak plainly, or I will make you.
scene_direction

The steward’s bow does not break.

“His Grace is in the east hall. He has been expecting you.” His thumb rests on the tray’s edge. “The doors will close at the ninth bell.”

A low chord rolls from somewhere behind the wall. Glass in the hallway shivers.

Chadwick, Leena, Vigil, Sodacan Bob, the pull behind your ribs sharpens. Four candles lean at once, though no air moves.

The steward’s face goes tight.

“Come in, please. Before the manor finishes deciding.”
character_reply
East hall. You lead. If the manor decides anything else, I decide first.
scene_direction

The steward turns first. His boots make no sound on wet stone. He leads you down a corridor lined with black doors. Each door opens a hand’s width as he passes. No hinges move.

Chadwick, Leena, Vigil, Sodacan Bob, the pull behind your ribs tightens. The candles ahead burn blue at the edge. A chair scrapes in the east hall, though the hall is closed.

The steward stops at a double door of oak and iron. He sets the tray on a side table. The tray hums.

“His Grace will see you,” he says. “But something else has asked to be seen first.”
character_reply
East hall, then. Let it come through that door, or not. But it will not make me kneel.
scene_direction

The double doors open.

The east hall is a great hall. Three hundred guests stand around long tables. Candles fill the ceiling. Music starts, then stops.

Chadwick, Leena, Vigil, Sodacan Bob, the pull behind your ribs turns sharp.

A crack runs up the nearest wall. Dust falls from the beams. Three black-cloaked figures step through the side arches. Iron pikes catch candlelight. Their faces are hidden.

The steward falls back. His silver tray tips.

“His Grace is not ready,” he says. “They came early.”

The nearest pike points at the four of you.
character_reply
Who sent you? Say it plain, or I will make you.
scene_direction

The manor doors open onto a long hall. Candles burn low. A harp plays by the stair.

Chadwick, Leena, Vigil, and Bob stand near the entrance. Each holds a heavy card. Leto’s seal is pressed deep in black wax.

The four look at one another. No one knows the others’ names. Something old presses against the back of their throats.

A serving girl drops a tray. Glass cuts the floor. The harp stops.

From the east wing comes a crash, then a scream. Doors fly open. Armed men in grey run into the hall. Their leader points a blade at the Duke.

“Take the guests,” he says. “Burn it down.”
character_reply
Guests behind me. You’ll burn nothing.
scene_direction

The blade stops an inch from the Duke’s throat.

The Duke does not flinch. His hand rises. Black light rings the floor. Grey men freeze mid-step. The leader spits.

“Guests first.”

He nods to his men. Three turn toward Chadwick. Two cut off the stair. One blocks the hall door.

The harp string snaps. A candle gutters out.

Chadwick, Leena, Vigil, Bob: the Duke’s eyes find you.

“Do not let them reach the east wing,” he says.
character_reply
Stair, door, east wing. Three jobs. No one dies until they try me.
scene_direction

Black light holds the grey men still. Their boots stop. Their blades stay up.

A hairline crack opens in the east wing wall. Dust drops. An old hum rises under the floor, low as a struck bell. The candles lean toward it.

The Duke’s hand trembles once. “That room must not open,” he says.

At the stair, the two grey men snap free. At the hall door, the third turns and swings. Chadwick, Leena, Vigil, Bob: three doors, one crash, one humming wall. Which of you moves first?
character_reply
Vigil, the stair. Bob, the door. I take the east wing. This is the way.
